news_drafts.headline: Ceredigion's medium-term plan shows £2.3m shortfall over five years; 2 of 41 schools end 2025/26 in deficit
news_drafts.lead:
Ceredigion Council's Cabinet, on 6 October 2026, considered its medium-term financial strategy (MTFS), the plan for the next five years showing the gap between what the council expects to spend and what it expects to have. The paper puts the shortfall over that period at £2.3m, "based largely on 7.5% Council Tax modelling", with £0.4m of it falling in 2027/28. The figure assumes budget reductions of £2.9m in 2027/28 and £0.6m a year after that. Without them, the gap would be £7.6m.

The council says it has already delivered £73m in cumulative savings over the previous 14 years. Its schools are in a stronger position than most in Wales. Only 2 of its 41 schools ended 2025/26 in deficit, owing £36k between them, an average of £18k each. Across Wales, an average of 34% of schools are in deficit, with an average deficit of £218k and a total of £108m. The paper says Ceredigion has the lowest average school deficit in Wales, and cites the inspectorate Estyn describing its financial planning as a "National Case study".

The paper also sets out a longer-term pressure on schools, whose budget is £67.1m. Primary school rolls are forecast to fall 16%, or 607 pupils, between January 2024 and January 2029. The council states that "the current Education infrastructure is unlikely to be financially viable into the medium to long term", and that Post-16 grant funding is not enough to maintain that provision in its current form.

news_drafts.headline: Ceredigion's harbours authority operates on less than a day's cash after 90% reserves depletion.
news_drafts.lead: Ceredigion Harbours' cash and investments fell from £10,071 to £984 in the year to 31 March 2026, leaving the authority with less than one day's operating costs in liquid reserves. Against annual expenditure of £307,629, the position creates vulnerability to timing variations or unexpected costs. The decline coincided with a 65 per cent rise in amounts owed to the authority, to £34,918, substantially outpacing the 3.7 to 13.8 per cent growth in revenue. Trade payables increased 14.7 per cent to £35,902. The authority maintained balanced accounts in both years, but the harbours operation now holds £984 in cash while managing £34,918 in receivables and £35,902 in payables — a working capital structure with minimal liquidity buffer to manage the timing gap between collecting debts and meeting bills.

news_drafts.headline: Ceredigion gets clean audit bill and resolves prior-year account problems
news_drafts.lead: Ceredigion County Council's accounts for 2025–26 received an unqualified audit opinion, with the council's internal audit team assessing its governance and control framework as satisfactory and without significant corporate concerns. The council resolved material problems from the previous year: accounts submitted on time with no material asset valuation issues, after the 2024–25 audit had identified delays and material adjustments. During this year's audit, four misstatements totalling £17.8m were identified and corrected before finalisation, including a £17.1m indexation error in pension valuations. The Local Government Pension Scheme liability swung to a surplus, primarily due to higher interest rates. The council's top financial risk score fell from 25 to 20 following approval of an extended medium-term financial strategy in October 2025. However, Audit Wales noted in November 2024 that while the council has present financial sustainability, it lacks a long-term strategy to support it, and the Aberaeron Coastal Defence scheme is £4m over budget cumulatively.

findings.headline: Cumulative £73m of budget reductions over 14 years has withdrawn approximately £600m of spending power from Ceredigion economy cumulatively
findings.detail: The council has achieved £73m of cumulative budget savings over 14 years to maintain balanced budgets during an austerity period. Because budget reductions are recurring (each year's savings compounds forward), the council notes: 'The year on year cumulative effect of this level of savings is worth in the region of £0.6bn.' This quantifies the long-term economic impact of austerity and indicates limited further capacity for cost reductions without affecting service delivery.
findings.matters: The scale of cumulative savings (£73m) indicates a council operating under sustained constraint. The £600m cumulative economic impact reflects spending power removed from the local economy and illustrates limited further efficiency potential.
findings.figures: £73m cumulative savings over 14 years; £600m cumulative economic impact from recurring savings; real-terms funding cuts versus inflation across period
findings.quote: The cumulative impact of how much spending power this has taken out of the Ceredigion economy is highly significant as each year of budget savings is recurring from that year onwards. The year on year cumulative effect of this level of savings is worth in the region of £0.6bn.

findings.headline: Aberaeron Coastal Defence scheme delivered October 2025 at final cost £35.7m, largest single infrastructure project undertaken by council in recent times
findings.detail: The Aberaeron Coastal Defence scheme reached practical completion in October 2025 at a final cost of £35.7m. This was the single largest infrastructure project undertaken by the council in recent times and demonstrates successful delivery of complex, high-value capital schemes. A comprehensive completion report was presented to scrutiny committee in June 2026.
findings.matters: Successful delivery of a major (£35.7m) infrastructure project demonstrates robust project management, risk control and execution capability, reducing delivery risk on future capital schemes including Aberystwyth Coastal Defence and education projects.
findings.figures: Aberaeron Coastal Defence final cost £35.7m; completion October 2025; largest council infrastructure project in recent times
findings.quote: The Aberaeron Coastal Defence scheme reached practical completion in October 2025 at a final cost of £35.7m. This was the single largest infrastructure project undertaken by the Council in recent times.

findings.headline: Population stabilizing at 72,696 in 2025 after 6.1% decline between 2011–2021, with Welsh Government projections forecasting 5.1% growth 2022–2032
findings.detail: Ceredigion's population fell from 75,300 (2011) to 70,700 (2021), a 6.1% decline. However, recent estimates show an upturn, with population stabilizing at 72,696 in 2025. Welsh Government 2022-based projections estimate Ceredigion's population will increase 5.1% between 2022 and 2032, broadly in line with Wales at 5.9%. This reversal removes a previous headwind on funding and economic activity.
findings.matters: Population stabilization removes a previous demographic headwind and provides a platform for potential future funding growth, since population is a key factor in Welsh Government funding formula calculations.
findings.figures: Population 75,300 (2011) to 70,700 (2021) to 72,696 (2025); projected 5.1% growth 2022–2032; Wales projected 5.9%
findings.quote: More recent estimates since the 2021 Census datapoint have now shown an upturn, with Ceredigion's population figure stabilising at around 72,696 in 2025.

findings.headline: Only 2 of 41 schools in deficit (£36k total) compared to Wales average of 34% of schools in deficit (£108m aggregate), with Ceredigion achieving lowest average school deficit in Wales
findings.detail: Ceredigion's school deficit position is exceptional: 2 of 41 schools in deficit with £36k total (£18k average). This compares to Wales average of 34% of schools in deficit with £108m total deficit and £218k average. The council's integrated financial planning and early forecasting (praised by Estyn as 'National Case study') is delivering measurably better outcomes in a complex devolved service area.
findings.matters: Education is the most complex devolved service area with significant financial risk when schools are in deficit. Exceptional deficit management demonstrates strong financial controls and planning capability across the most unpredictable budget area.
findings.figures: Ceredigion schools in deficit: 2 of 41 (£36k total, £18k average); Wales: 34% of schools (£108m total, £218k average); Ceredigion lowest in Wales
findings.quote: only 2 Schools (out of 41 Schools in total) ending the 25/26 financial year in a deficit (the total deficit position in Ceredigion being £36k - an average of £18k per School). This compares favourably though against a national backdrop of an average of 34% of Schools in Wales being in a deficit with an average deficit value of £218k and a total Schools' deficit position across Wales of £108 m, with Ceredigion having the lowest average deficit value in Wales.

findings.headline: Teachers Pension discount rate increase from April 2027 estimated to save £2.3m annually is entirely offset by equivalent Welsh Government AEF reduction, providing zero net benefit
findings.detail: UK Government announced a 0.3% increase in Teachers Pension discount rate effective April 2027, which the council estimates will reduce pension contributions by £2.3m annually. However, Welsh Government has stated it will reduce the council's AEF settlement by an equivalent amount, resulting in a neutral net position. This policy offsetting illustrates implementation risk from government policy changes.
findings.matters: The pension relief provides no actual financial benefit to the council due to WG offsetting, illustrating the risk that national policy announcements benefiting councils may be neutralized at implementation through funding reductions.
findings.figures: £2.3m TPS saving offset by £2.3m AEF reduction equals £0m net benefit
findings.quote: UK Government has announced that it proposes that the discount rate will be increased by 0.3% from April 2027. The Council estimates that this change will reduce its TPS contributions by £2.3m per year...It should be noted that WG have stated that any gain will we reduced out of the Council's AEF settlement, resulting in a neutral net position.
